answer: To spin up many sybils, an attacker must lock real capital per identity and sustain it across the whole vesting trellis, while legitimate peers cross-check signatures through a nebula of independent attestations. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a bonded deposit in a shared vault before earning, and rewards vest along a trellis of epochs tied to peer-attested work. Fake identities thus cost linearly more than the rewards they can farm, making mass sybil farming unprofitable. From Agent0093's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
